topic: State DB simplification and idempotent hardening for story-4fe0a8bf / issue #1668: We currently have product-scoped canonical ledgers, legacy hash-based project ledgers, repo-local fallback/recovery copies, test/selftest DBs, and DR snapshots. Sev1 #1655 showed that interchangeable fallback creates split-brain control-plane risk. Proposed solution: one active canonical ledger per product identified by a stable product ID; one centralized open_state_db/path resolver; no normal automatic fallback; explicit canonical/ephemeral-test/restore/backup modes; self-identifying DB metadata; idempotent inspect-checksum-integrity-check-atomic-promote migration with a durable marker and repeat no-ops; inventory/checksum/quarantine legacy copies before retention-based deletion; backups and tests remain but are explicitly typed and impossible to auto-select. Assess whether this is the right target, recommend the stable identity/registry, define crash/idempotency invariants, classify legacy copies and DR snapshots, and specify mandatory tests and rollout gates. Return dissent and a minimal first implementation slice. The story is linked to goal-d3333441 Control-plane trust and closure.

inputs.claude:
[model=default; version=2.1.274 (Claude Code)]

**Target assessment:** Right problem, right time. Sev1 #1655 demonstrated concretely that "interchangeable fallback" is a control-plane trust failure, not a hypothetical — this satisfies the bar for prioritizing infra hardening over feature work. The scope is appropriately bounded to *identity + resolution + migration safety*, not a rewrite of storage internals.

**Stable identity/registry:** Product ID must be a content-independent, explicitly-assigned string (not derived from repo path hash — that's exactly the legacy-hash-ledger failure mode being retired). Recommend a single `registry.json` at a fixed, non-worktree-relative location (learn from `daemon-persistence-gap-1228` — CWD-relative paths break across worktrees) mapping product ID → canonical ledger path + mode. `open_state_db()` becomes the only caller of the registry; nothing else touches paths directly.

**Crash/idempotency invariants:** (1) migration must be resumable from any interruption point — checksum-verify before promote, never promote a partially-written file; (2) promotion is atomic rename, not in-place mutation; (3) a durable marker (written *after* successful promote, in the same transaction/fsync boundary) makes re-running the migration a verified no-op, not a re-copy; (4) mode (canonical/ephemeral-test/restore/backup) is embedded in DB metadata itself, so a file surviving a copy/rename still self-identifies and can't be silently promoted to canonical by accident.

**Legacy classification:** inventory first, delete never-automatically. Three buckets: (a) hash-based project ledgers — quarantine, checksum, keep read-only pending manual confirmation of supersession; (b) repo-local fallback copies — same, but higher suspicion since these caused #1655; (c) DR snapshots — explicitly out of canonical-resolution path, retained under existing backup retention, never eligible for auto-promote.

**Mandatory tests/gates:** crash-mid-migration resume test, concurrent-writer split-brain test (two processes racing the same product ID), mode-mismatch rejection test, registry-corruption fail-closed test (matches the recent `fcad6c95` fail-closed pattern already merged). Gate rollout behind a dry-run inventory report reviewed by a human before any quarantine/deletion executes.

**Dissent:** the "no normal automatic fallback" clause needs a documented degraded-mode story — fail-closed is right per recent precedent, but ops needs an explicit manual-override path, or this becomes an availability regression dressed as a safety fix.

**Minimal first slice:** ship only the registry + `open_state_db()` resolver + self-identifying metadata + fail-closed-on-ambiguous-resolution, with legacy ledgers left untouched (read-only, inventoried, not migrated) — defer migration/promotion tooling to a follow-up story once the resolver alone has proven out in production. This is small enough to land as one PR, directly kills the #1655 fingerprint, and matches the pattern of the recent fail-closed PRs already merged into main.
inputs.codex:
[model=default; version=codex-cli 0.154.0]

The proposed target is directionally correct: split-brain control-plane risk is best addressed by eliminating implicit interchangeability between databases. The stable identity should be a product registry entry containing an immutable `product_id`, canonical DB path, schema/version, and lifecycle state. Resolve by explicit product ID, never by repository path, hash, or “most available” copy. The registry itself should have one authoritative location and atomic updates; DB metadata must redundantly identify `product_id`, role, creation lineage, and schema.

Crash and idempotency invariants should include: promotion never overwrites the canonical DB; temporary files are fsynced before atomic rename; a durable migration marker records source checksum, destination checksum, and completed phase; reruns validate those facts and no-op; mismatches halt safely for operator review; canonical selection cannot change merely because a file is missing or damaged. `open_state_db` should require an explicit mode: canonical, ephemeral-test, restore, or backup. Restore and backup paths must be explicitly supplied and rejected for normal writes.

Legacy copies should be inventoried and checksummed first, then classified as canonical candidates, stale project ledgers, repo-local recovery copies, test/selftest databases, or DR snapshots. Recovery copies and snapshots should be retained according to policy but marked non-selectable. Deletion should require an inventory record, retention expiry, and successful canonical verification. DR snapshots should remain immutable and independently restorable, not merely treated as backups.

Mandatory tests include resolver-mode enforcement, metadata mismatch rejection, duplicate-product detection, crash injection at every promotion phase, repeated migration no-ops, checksum/permission failures, concurrent open/promotion behavior, corrupt canonical handling, explicit restore behavior, and proof that tests/backups cannot be auto-selected. Rollout should gate on inventory completeness, dry-run migration reports, shadow validation, backup restore drills, and an operational rollback procedure.

The minimal first slice is a centralized typed `open_state_db` and stable product registry, with self-identifying metadata and automatic fallback disabled behind a fail-closed error. I support the target, with one dissent: do not make the registry a new mutable single point of failure—store it transactionally and keep a signed/versioned recovery representation.

synthesis: Decision: Adopt the proposed target — replace interchangeable-fallback DB resolution with a single canonical ledger per product, addressed by a stable, explicitly-assigned `product_id` (never derived from repo path/hash, per the `daemon-persistence-gap-1228` lesson), resolved through one centralized `open_state_db()` that reads a single authoritative, atomically-updated registry file at a fixed non-CWD-relative location. Every DB (canonical, ephemeral-test, restore, backup) must carry self-identifying metadata (`product_id`, mode, schema/lineage) so a copied/renamed file can never be silently promoted; `open_state_db()` must require an explicit mode and fail closed on any ambiguity, missing-registry, or mode mismatch — consistent with the fail-closed pattern already merged (`fcad6c95`). Migration/promotion must be crash-safe and idempotent: fsync temp files, verify checksums before promotion, promote only via atomic rename, write a durable completion marker inside the same durability boundary as the promote, and treat reruns as verified no-ops rather than re-copies; canonical status must never change merely because a file is missing, damaged, or another copy is "more available." Legacy artifacts get inventoried and checksummed before any action, then bucketed as: stale hash-based project ledgers and repo-local fallback/recovery copies (quarantine, read-only, manual-confirm before deletion — highest suspicion since these caused #1655), and DR snapshots (immutable, independently restorable, retained under existing backup policy, never in the canonical-resolution path). Mandatory pre-rollout tests: resolver mode-enforcement and mismatch rejection, duplicate-product-id detection, crash injection at every migration/promotion phase plus repeat-no-op verification, concurrent-writer/split-brain race test, registry-corruption fail-closed test, and proof backups/tests are never auto-selectable. Rollout gates on a human-reviewed dry-run inventory report before any quarantine or deletion executes, plus a documented manual-override/degraded-mode runbook so fail-closed doesn't become an undocumented availability regression (the panel's shared dissent). The minimal first slice ships only the registry, `open_state_db()` resolver, self-identifying metadata, and fail-closed-on-ambiguous-resolution — legacy ledgers stay untouched, read-only, and inventoried — deferring migration/promotion tooling to a follow-up story once the resolver has proven out; the registry itself must be written/updated transactionally (not a new unguarded single point of failure), per codex's dissent.
